title: Apostolic rite and polity left to the Church — under order and decency
source_text: XXXIV. Praeterea quoque asserimus, ea, quae ab Apostolis instituta fuerunt circa ritus divini cultus, & Ecclesiastici regiminis circumstantias, & de quibus tamen Scripturae sacrae silent, esse potestati Ecclesiae permissa, ut ea, pro temporum & locorum ratione, varie immutare posset, sub hac tantum regula & cautione generali, ut omnia fiant ordine & decenter in Ecclesia Dei.
pass_a_gloss: Besides we also assert that those things which were instituted by the Apostles concerning the rites of divine worship and the circumstances of Ecclesiastical government, and about which nevertheless the sacred Scriptures are silent, were committed to the power of the Church, so that it might variously change them according to the reason of times and places, under this general rule and caution only, that all things be done in order and decently in the Church of God.
pass_b_english: We also assert that what the Apostles instituted about rites of divine worship and circumstances of church government — where sacred Scripture is silent — was left to the Church's power.
She may change those things variously for times and places, under this general rule alone: that all things be done in order and decently in the Church of God (1 Cor. 14:40).

lemmas.gloss: committed / left to the Church's power

choices.why: Permission of power, not that Scripture forbids change.
